text:
Situation: The amino acid injection from B. Braun Medical Inc. remains in shortage. Corvale East holds 10 units, providing 2.5 days of supply at a daily use of 4.1 units. Corvale General holds 64 units (14.6 days). Corvale Lakeside holds 30 units (25.9 days).

Why: FDA's shortage list shows the amino acid injection from B. Braun Medical Inc. has been in Current status since its initial posting on 2020-12-08. As of 2026-10-21 the shortage has been on FDA's list for 70 months.

Our position: Internal transfer from the site with the highest days of supply is the fastest way to protect Corvale East without new procurement.

Recommended actions:
1. Transfer 13 units of the 0.82 g/100 mL + 1.4 g/100 mL + 1.2 g/100 mL + 0.34 g/100 mL + 0.48 g/100 mL + 0.42 g/100 mL + 0.2 g/100 mL + 0.78 g/100 mL + 0.024 g/100 mL + 0.48 g/100 mL + 0.044 g/100 mL + 0.24 g/100 mL + 0.54 g/100 mL + 1.2 g/100 mL + 0.68 g/100 mL + 0.38 g/100 mL + 0.36 g/100 mL + 0.32 g/100 mL + 0.5 g/100 mL + 0.025 g/100 mL, 500 mL solution from Corvale Lakeside to Corvale East. Approval required: Pharmacy Director (transfer request).
2. If Option 1 cannot be executed, transfer 2 units of the same formulation from Corvale General to Corvale East. Approval required: Pharmacy Director (transfer request).

Not recommended: No other transfers or purchases at this time.
